title: Spot the bug: topology

predict.test: Claim 2 on Sierpiński space: every continuous bijection to itself has a continuous inverse
predict.statement: Every continuous bijection from Sierpiński space to itself has a continuous inverse.

public: Claim 1: f₁ is continuous from discrete 2 to Sierpiński space
Claim 3: x and y are different

questions.text: True or false: `SamContAt (fun _ => 0) 1` holds, that is, Sam's definition says that the constant function `0` is continuous at `1`.

checks.lean:
#check (L47.f₁ : Fin 2 → Fin 2)
#check (L47.f₂ : Fin 2 → Fin 2)
#check (L47.g : Fin 2 → Fin 2)
#check (L47.p : Fin 2)
#check (L47.x : Fin 2)
#check (L47.y : Fin 2)
#check (L47.q1 : Bool)
checks.message: Keep the maps `f₁ f₂ g : Fin 2 → Fin 2`, the points `p x y : Fin 2` and the answer `q1 : Bool`.

steps: Every map out of a discrete space is continuous. Look for one whose image of `{0}` isn't open in Sierpiński space.
hints.hint: `f₁ = id`, written `fun i => i`. The image of the open set `{0}` is `{0}`, which isn't open in Sierpiński space.

steps: Every set is open in `discrete 2`, so Sam's definition accepts any map out of Sierpiński space. Which map pulls `{0}` back to a non-open set?
hints.hint: `f₂ = fun i => i`. The preimage of `{0}` is `{0}`, which isn't open in Sierpiński space.

steps: Any bijection out of a discrete space is continuous. Is its image of `{0}` open?
hints.hint: `g = fun i => i`. It's continuous, but the image of the open set `{0}` is `{0}`.

steps: The only open set containing `0` is the whole space. Which point lies in every open set containing `1`?
hints.hint: `p = 1`, `x = 0`, `y = 1`. Every open set containing `0` or `1` contains `1`.
For a constant function, the preimage of a small neighbourhood of `1` (one that misses `0`) is `∅`, and `∅` is not a neighbourhood of `0`.
